coreIdea: Node+pointer chain. No random access (search=O(n)). Insert/delete=O(1) ONCE you have the position/pointer.
mustRememberFormulas: Insert/delete with pointer in hand: O(1); finding that pointer by value: O(n)
Singly-list delete given only the node's own pointer: O(1) via copy-next-delete-next trick, FAILS for last node
Doubly-list delete given the node's own pointer: always true O(1)
Circular queue: point single external pointer to REAR (front = rear->next, both O(1))

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: C code modifying list pointers, asked for resulting list

circular list, single external pointer, which node to point to

commonTrapsQuickList: O(1) deletion trick (copy-next, delete-next) FAILS for the last node
Binary search on a linked list is NOT O(log n) — no random access
Doubly linked list delete-given-pointer is ALWAYS O(1); singly is conditional
Never assume linked list is 'better' or 'worse' than array in general — always operation-specific
highYieldPyqLessons: Code-tracing (8/24) is the default skill — draw boxes and arrows, update one statement at a time, every single time.
The 'last node' edge case breaks more tricks (O(1) deletion, circular-pointer design) than any other single edge case — always check for it explicitly.
